issue_context.title: Annoying sounds
issue_context.body:
### Check for existing issues - [X] Completed ### Describe the bug / provide steps to reproduce it The zed makes an annoying beep when a certain key is entered. Is there an option to turn it off ### Environment win10 ### If applicable, add mockups / screenshots to help explain present your vision of the feature _No response_ ### If applicable, attach your Zed.log file to this issue.
Zed.log
comments:
> when a certain key is entered

How are people supposed to reproduce this?
Please add more details — which file are you in, what are you pressing, etc.
Logs and videos are also very welcome, same as description of

> an annoying beep

it's not Zed's one so most probably comes out of your system.

> win10

To note, Windows is not officially supported yet, and only certain, few, external contributors deal with Windows code.
So most probably this will stay not fixed for a while.
As an idea, I would ensure that there are no Windows-specific bindings to the same "a certain key is entered".

hi，like this,when i bing alt-x to this command, and i clicked alt-x,the command will be done,but also has the sound at the same time. Several of the commands I've bound have done this, and I think it should be easy to reproduce

I wonder if that's what you're hitting.
https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/keyboard-shortcuts-for-international-characters-108fa0c1-fb8e-4aae-9db1-d60407d13c35

```
The Unicode character for the specified Unicode (hexadecimal) character code
	

The character code, ALT+X

For example, to insert the euro currency symbol , press 20AC, and then hold down the ALT key and press X.
```

So, you press something, then press alt-x and whatever was pressed before is attempted to be parsed as a Unicode character, invalid ergo the beep.

Have you tried changing the shortcut or repeating the same sequence of actions in e.g. a Notepad.exe?
Thanks for the answer, but that's not the case. I found that the alt key connected to any key comes out with this tone
Windows treats the `alt + key` combination as a shortcut. If Windows thinks it is not properly handled, it will beep. I will create a PR to address this issue.
Do I need to close this issue?

> Do I need to close this issue?

No, it will be closed when the PR is merged.
